newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia plans to sign gas sell-off deal in March.
newsitem.headline: Latvia plans to sign gas sell-off deal in March.

text.p: Latvia is certain that it will sign a privatisation deal for its national gas company in March with both German Ruhrgas and Preussen and Russian Gazprom, the head of the privatisation agency said on Wednesday.
"We will be able to sign the agreement in March with both the Germans and the Russians on a single day," agency head Janis Naglis told a news conference.
The deal for around 30 percent stake in Latvian Gas was planned to be signed late last year but has been postponed three times as the German firms were worried over Latvian Gas's debts.
"A group of Preussen and Ruhrgas specialists is to arrive in Riga next week to conclude talks and finalise the date of the signing," Naglis added.
Ruhrgas and Preussen formed a consortium to buy a stake in Latvian Gas with Gazprom as a separate partner.
The government earlier promised the German side to either write off or capitalise a part of the company's debts, although it was a smaller amount than demanded by the German consortium.

"Telephone conversations with Gazprom also show that they are all ready for a journey to Riga (to sign a deal)," Naglis added. Gazprom delayed its signing as it was also worried about the size of the company's debts.
